subject: Hosted API pilot — access coordination, endpoints & rate checks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Carl Monroe <carl@finlytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API pilot — access coordination, endpoints & rate checks

Hi Carl,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through FinLytics' inference use cases. Per our demo, this thread is a short checklist so we can get your hosted pilot (Hosted API) provisioned and avoid surprises on rate limits or rollout. Please confirm the bold items below or reply with edits.

Summary of asks from the call:
- Confirm you'd like to run a Hosted API pilot (vs Dedicated or Private) for the next 30 days. Hosted is simplest for fast feedback; Dedicated starts to make sense when steady peak sustained throughput > ~700k tokens/day or strict data isolation is required.
- Provide a small traffic profile: expected average requests per second, typical prompt lengths (tokens in / out), and peak minute RPS you expect during demo spikes.
- Do you have a latency SLO for interactive features? (e.g., 200ms p50, 500ms p95)
- Procurement contact for a short MOU and demo access (we'll send a DocuSign).

What Redwood will do for the pilot (quickstart):
1) Create a staging API key and a staging endpoint (scoped to FinLytics) — usually ready within 1 business day after we receive the traffic profile and MOU.
2) Apply a pilot rate policy: default 60 RPM / 1K tokens with a temporary burst window (we can raise to 120 RPM for the demo). If you need a higher baseline for the whole pilot, tell us the numbers.
3) Provide the quickstart PDF attached (hosted-pilot-quickstart.pdf) with examples, recommended batching, and SDK snippets.
4) Share a short rate_profile.csv template (we'll ask you to fill it) so our infra team can pre-configure canary endpoints.

Decision guidance (short):
- Pick Hosted if you want fastest onboarding and don't require a dedicated GPU pool or VPC.
- Pick Dedicated if you need reserved throughput and a contract-backed SLA for p95 latency or data isolation.
- Pick Private only if you require VPC-only access or on-premise deployment due to compliance.

Next steps (proposed):
- Carl: send the traffic profile and procurement point-of-contact by EOD Friday.
- Redwood (Sean & Soojin): provision staging key and send DocuSign pilot MOU once POC is assigned.

I'm CC'ing Sean (ops) to support rate-caps and traffic pre-wiring.

Thanks — looking forward to a quick pilot.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Mid-Market
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: hosted-pilot-quickstart.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)
From: Carl Monroe <carl@finlytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pilot — access coordination, endpoints & rate checks

Thanks Soojin — useful checklist. We want to proceed with Hosted for the pilot (we like the speed of onboarding). Quick answers below and a couple of clarifying questions.

Traffic profile (initial):
- Typical concurrency: 8 TPS average during business hours (PST)
- Peak minute: ~60 RPS during batch scoring runs (30–60 seconds)
- Average prompt tokens in: 120 tokens; average completion tokens out: 140 tokens
- Expected token volume for 30-day pilot: ~1.2M tokens/day (estimate)

Latency SLO: interactive features should aim for p95 < 600ms; p50 under 220ms is nice-to-have.

Questions:
1) Can you provide a staging endpoint (non-production) matching the same model family so we can run parallel tests?
2) For the rate caps you suggested, will temporary demo bursts be applied automatically or do we need to request them before demo windows?

Procurement: procurement@finlytics.com (please send the MOU there).

Appreciate it — Carl

Subject: Re: Hosted API pilot — access coordination, endpoints & rate checks

Looping in some quick ops guidance based on Carl's profile. Summary below — happy to spin up the staging endpoints once we have the filled rate_profile.csv.

Notes / recommendations:
- Staging endpoint: yes — we can mirror the model family and provide a dedicated staging hostname (staging-api.redwood.com/finlytics). That endpoint will emulate production routing and kernel selection; p95 may vary slightly from hosted production but is reliable for validation.
- Rate policy: baseline 60 RPM / 1K tokens is conservative. With your peak minute of ~60 RPS and 1.2M tokens/day, I'd recommend we pre-configure a pilot policy: baseline 200 RPM / 5K tokens with a temporary demo burst of 500 RPM for a 10-minute window tied to a signed MOU. That avoids token throttles during short spikes.
- Batching: please enable client-side batching in the SDK for bulk scoring. We recommend batch size 8–16 for your prompt sizes to reduce per-token cost.
- Canary plan: we'll create two endpoints: staging (for validation) and canary (for demo ramp). We'll route small % of traffic to canary and scale quickly if all checks pass.

Attachment: rate-profile.csv (CSV template)

If you want, Sean and I can run a 30-minute pre-demo run with your engineers to validate end-to-end and confirm p95 numbers.

Thanks,
Aditya
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
